newsitem.title: BELGIUM: PS ACCOUNTANT ARRESTED IN DASSAULT BRIBE PROBE.
newsitem.headline: PS ACCOUNTANT ARRESTED IN DASSAULT BRIBE PROBE.

text.p: Belgian police have arrested the former accountant of Belgium's francophone Socialist Party (PS) in connection with an investigation of allegations that French aerospace group Dassault paid bribes to Belgian political parties, the PS said on Friday.

The arrest of Fernand Detaille is the third in connection with the Dassault probe. Two former top PS officials, Merry Hermanus and Francois Pirot, were arrested last month and charged with corruption.
The Liege public prosecutor's office was not immediately available for comment on Detaille's arrest.
The arrests of Hermanus and Pirot have rattled the government and sparked a leadership crisis in the PS, the most powerful party in the French-speakiing southern half of Belgium.

Belgium's four-party coalition government easily won a series of confidence votes in parliament late on Thursday after its members patched up differences earlier in the week over the corruption scandal and voted together.
The votes were won by 80 votes against 59, representing the respective sizes of the centre-left coalition and the main opposition.
BRTN radio said police discovered during searches at the PS headquarters that the party's accounts for 1989 and 1990 had disappeared. They were later found in Detaille's office.
The Belgian judiciary is investigating claims that Dassault paid kickbacks to Belgian parties to secure a 1989 contract to fit air defence systems to the country's F-16 fighter jets.
Dassault has always denied any wrongdoing.
Lawyers for the two PS officials have said that Hermanus and Pirot accepted 30 million francs (about $1 million) from Dassault for the PS.

Last May, the Belgian judiciary issued an international arrest warrant for Serge Dassault, group founder and chairman of Dassault Aviation, who has denied all wrongdoing but has refused to come to Belgium to answer questions relating to the affair.
